A BMP session ends when the TCP session that carries it is closed for any reason.

intro.quote: Once a connection is established, the router sends messages over it. There is no initialization or handshaking phase, messages are simply sent as soon as the connection is established.

steps.explain: The router sends an Initiation message first after the BMP session comes up.

cite.quote: It MUST begin by sending an Initiation message.

steps.explain: For each monitored BGP peer already in the Established state, the router reports that the peer is up.

cite.quote: It subsequently sends a Peer Up message over the BMP session for each of its monitored BGP peers that is in the Established state.

steps.explain: The monitored peers' Adj-RIB-In routes are carried in standard BGP Update messages inside Route Monitoring messages.

cite.quote: This is done by sending all routes stored in the Adj-RIB-In of those peers using standard BGP Update messages, encapsulated in Route Monitoring messages.

steps.explain: The router marks the end of the initial route dump for that peer.

steps.explain: After the initial table dump, the router sends incremental updates in Route Monitoring messages.

intro.quote: The following common header appears in all BMP messages. The rest of the data in a BMP message is dependent on the Message Type field in the common header.

fields.name: Version
fields.explain: Identifies the BMP version. Messages defined by this specification use version 3, while version 0 is reserved.

cite.quote: Version (1 byte): Indicates the BMP version. This is set to '3' for all messages defined in this specification. ('1' and '2' were used by draft versions of this document.) Version 0 is reserved and MUST NOT be sent.

fields.name: Message Length
fields.explain: Gives the length of the complete message in bytes, including headers, data, and any encapsulated messages.

cite.quote: Message Length (4 bytes): Length of the message in bytes (including headers, data, and encapsulated messages, if any).

fields.name: Message Type
fields.explain: Identifies the kind of BMP message. Implementations ignore message types they do not recognize.

cite.quote: Message Type (1 byte): This identifies the type of the BMP message. A BMP implementation MUST ignore unrecognized message types upon receipt.

intro.quote: The per-peer header follows the common header for most BMP messages. The rest of the data in a BMP message is dependent on the Message Type field in the common header.

cite.quote: Peer Type (1 byte): Identifies the type of peer.

fields.name: Peer Flags
fields.explain: Provides more information about the peer.

cite.quote: Peer Flags (1 byte): These flags provide more information about the peer.

fields.name: Peer Distinguisher
fields.explain: Distinguishes peers that belong to different address domains on routers that support multiple instances.

cite.quote: Peer Distinguisher (8 bytes): Routers today can have multiple instances (example: Layer 3 Virtual Private Networks (L3VPNs) [RFC4364]). This field is present to distinguish peers that belong to one address domain from the other.

fields.name: Peer Address
fields.explain: Holds the remote IP address associated with the TCP session, with the most significant bytes zero-filled for an IPv4 address.

cite.quote: Peer Address: The remote IP address associated with the TCP session over which the encapsulated PDU was received. It is 4 bytes long if an IPv4 address is carried in this field (with the 12 most significant bytes zero-filled) and 16 bytes long if an IPv6 address is carried in this field.

fields.name: Peer AS
fields.explain: Holds the peer's Autonomous System number, with a 16-bit AS number padded in the most significant bits.

cite.quote: Peer AS: The Autonomous System number of the peer from which the encapsulated PDU was received. If a 16-bit AS number is stored in this field [RFC6793], it should be padded with zeroes in the 16 most significant bits.

fields.name: Peer BGP ID
fields.explain: Holds the BGP Identifier of the peer from which the encapsulated PDU was received.

cite.quote: Peer BGP ID: The BGP Identifier of the peer from which the encapsulated PDU was received.

fields.name: Timestamp (seconds)
fields.explain: Records the seconds part of the time when the encapsulated routes were received or installed in the Adj-RIB-In.

cite.quote: Timestamp (seconds)

fields.name: Timestamp (microseconds)
fields.explain: Records the microseconds part of the time when the encapsulated routes were received or installed in the Adj-RIB-In.

cite.quote: Timestamp (microseconds)

intro.quote: Peer Flags (1 byte): These flags provide more information about the peer.

fields.name: V flag
fields.explain: Indicates that the Peer address is an IPv6 address and is zero for an IPv4 peer.

cite.quote: The V flag indicates that the Peer address is an IPv6 address. For IPv4 peers, this is set to 0.

fields.name: L flag
fields.explain: Set to 1 for the post-policy Adj-RIB-In and 0 for the pre-policy Adj-RIB-In; locally sourced routes also set it to 1.

cite.quote: The L flag, if set to 1, indicates that the message reflects the post-policy Adj-RIB-In (i.e., its path attributes reflect the application of inbound policy). It is set to 0 if the message reflects the pre-policy Adj-RIB-In. Locally sourced routes also carry an L flag of 1.

fields.name: A flag
fields.explain: Set to 1 when the legacy 2-byte AS_PATH format is used and 0 when the 4-byte AS_PATH format is used.

cite.quote: The A flag, if set to 1, indicates that the message is formatted using the legacy 2-byte AS_PATH format. If set to 0, the message is formatted using the 4-byte AS_PATH format [RFC6793].

fields.name: Reserved
fields.explain: Reserved for future use, transmitted as 0, and ignored on receipt.

cite.quote: The remaining bits are reserved for future use. They MUST be transmitted as 0 and their values MUST be ignored on receipt.

intro.quote: The Information TLV is used by the Initiation (Section 4.3) and Peer Up (Section 4.10) messages.

fields.name: Information Type
fields.explain: Identifies the type of information carried in the TLV.

cite.quote: Information Type (2 bytes): Type of information provided. Defined types are:

fields.name: Information
fields.explain: Carries information about the monitored router according to the Information Type.

cite.quote: Information (variable): Information about the monitored router, according to the type.

fields.name: Information Length
fields.explain: Gives the length of the following Information field in bytes.

cite.quote: Information Length (2 bytes): The length of the following Information field, in bytes.
